Though these appeals are listed for orders, with the consent of both counsel, they are taken up for final disposal.
2. MFA No.201130/2015 filed by appellants/claimants under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act,
1988 (for short 'the Act') seeking enhancement of compensation granted for the death of their father-Manik Jadhav in a motor vehicles accident.

sentences.text: 3 appellant/Sriram General Insurance Company, on the basis of quantum of compensation granted by the Tribunal.
3. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to by their rank before the Tribunal.
4. Petitioners are the children of deceased-Manik Jadhav.

It is the case of the petitioners that on 06.05.2012 at about 21:00 p.m. when the deceased was going by horse on the road from Andur to Naldurg, at that time, Mini lorry bearing Reg.No.MH-25/7940 came in a high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the Manik Jadhav and horse, who was sat on the body of the horse,
then fell down by the horse and caused injuries and died at Hospital during the treatment on 14.05.2012.
The accident caused due to rash and negligent act of the driver of mini lorry bearing Reg.No.MH-25/7940 (for short 'offending vehicle').
The respondent Nos.1 and 3 being the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle, liable to pay the compensation.
Hence, prayed to allow the petition.
5. Upon service of notice, respondent No.1 remained unrepresented and place ex parte before the Tribunal.
Before the Tribunal petition against respondent No.2/United India insurance company dismissed as not pressed.
6. Respondent No.3/Sriram General insurance company appeared and filed written statement denying the age, occupation, income of the deceased and also that petitioners were dependent on him.

It is further contended that the deceased-Manik Jadhav himself was riding horse in careless manner as such, he himself fell down from the horse and suffered injuries and he was responsible for his own death.
It is further submitted that the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving licence to drive such type of vehicle as on the date of accident.
On this ground, respondent No.3/insurance company cannot be liable to pay the compensation.

Hence,
prays to dismiss the petition.
7. Based on these pleadings, the Tribunal framed necessary issues.
8. On behalf of the petitioners, petitioner No.1 is examined as P.W.1 and Exs.P1 to 4 got marked.

On behalf of respondents, respondent No.3 examined its official as RW.1 and got marked Exs.R1 and 2.
9.

Vide the impugned judgment and award, the Tribunal has partly allowed the petition and quantified the compensation at Rs.6,00,000/- with interest at 6% per annum and directed respondent No.3/insurance company to pay the same.

10. The details of the compensation granted are as under:
 Sl. Head Amount awarded  No.
 1. Loss of dependency Rs.5,60,000/-

2 . Transportation of dead Rs.5,000/-
 body  3. Towards love and affection Rs.15,000/-
 4. Loss of estate Rs.10,000/-

sentences.text: During the course of argument, learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that the income taken at Rs.5,000/- p.m. which is on the lower side.
The Tribunal has not added future prospects to the income.
The compensation granted under other heads is also on the lower side, which requires enhancement.
Hence, prays to allow the appeal.

12. On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent contended that the alleged accident took place due to negligence of deceased as he was riding horse in careless manner as such, he himself fell down from horse and responsible for his own death and no vehicle was involved in the alleged accident.
It is further contended that the driver was not holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the vehicle as on the date of accident.
Hence, the impugned judgment of the Tribunal needs to be modified.

13. After hearing the arguments on both sides, the following points arise for consideration:
(i) Whether the petitioners/claimants in MFA No.201130/2015 are entitled for enhancement of compensation?
(ii) Whether the appellant/insurance company in MFA No.202011/2015 have made grounds to interfere with the impugned judgment and award?
( iii )
What order/award?

14. My findings on above points are as under:
(i) Point No.1 : In partly Affirmative (ii) Point No.2 : In Negative (iii) Point No.3 : As per final order for the following:
REASONS 15. Point No.1: Since the accident is of the year 2012, the income ought to have been taken at Rs.6,500/-
p.m. instead of Rs.5,000/- p.m.
The deceased was aged 40 years, the appropriate multiplier would be 15.
However, the Tribunal has not added any compensation towards loss of future prospects, as per National Insurance Co. Ltd., vs Pranay Sethi and Ors reported in 2017 (16) SCC 680

sentences.text: , 25% is required to be added towards loss of future prospects.

Therefore, the Shriram General Insurance Co.Ltd vs Mohan S/O Manik Jadhav on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196943367/
5 income is required to be taken at Rs.8,125/-.

sentences.text: Since there are three dependents, 1/3rd is required to be deducted towards his personal and living expenses.
With these components, the compensation under the head loss of dependency is Rs.8,125/- x12x15x2/3rd=Rs.9,75,060/- (rounded off to Rs.9,75,000/-) as against Rs.5,60,000/- granted by the Tribunal.

As children of deceased, petitioners are entitled for compensation in a sum of Rs.40,000/- each i.e., Rs.1,20,000/- under the head loss of consortium as per Magma General Insurance Company Limited Vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram And Others1.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Company Limited Vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram And Others1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Similarly, the compensation in a sum of Rs.15,000/- each is awarded towards loss of estate and funeral expenses including transportation of dead body.

17. Thus, in all petitioners are entitled for total compensation in a sum of Rs.11,25,000/- as against Rs.6,00,000/- granted by the Tribunal with interest at 6% per annum as detailed below:

2 . Transportation of dead Rs.5,000/- Rs.15,000/-
 body  Funeral and other Rs.10,000/-

4 . Loss of estate Rs.10,000/- Rs.15,000/-
 5. Loss of consortium ---- Rs.1,20,000/-
To this extent, the appeal filed by the petitioners in MFA No.201130/2015 requires to be modified and point No.1 is answered partly in Affirmative.
19. Point No.2:
Learned counsel for the appellant/Sriram General insurance company has contended that the Tribunal has utterly failed to appreciate the oral and documentary evidence on record.

Respondent Nos.1 to 3 have failed to prove issue Shriram General Insurance Co.Ltd vs Mohan S/O Manik Jadhav on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196943367/
6 No.1 i.e. they failed to prove that deceased-Manik Jadhav the father of claimants has died in the alleged accudent due to rash and negligent driving of lorry bearing Reg.No.MH-25/7940.

sentences.text:
The deceased was riding the horse and he himself fall from the horse and suffered injures and deceased himself solely responsible for his death,
therefore, the death of the deceased was not motor vehicle accidental death.
She further contended that after lapse of 27 days from the date of alleged accident, a false complaint was lodged to the police.
The claimants in collusion with the owner of the - 12 - vehicle and with the concerned police got falsely implicated the insured lorry in the alleged accident to get compensation.
There is no nexus between the said lorry and death of deceased-Manik.

20. Further learned counsel for appellant/insurance company further submitted that the driver of lorry bearing Reg.No.MH-25/7940 was not holding valid and effective driving licence to drive particular type of vehicle as on the date of the alleged accident.
No vehicle is involved in the alleged accident.
The insured lorry bearing Reg.No.MH- 25/7940 was not at all involved in the alleged accident.

The claimants in collusion with the owner of the vehicle i.e. respondent No.4 and with the concerned police got falsely implicated the insured above said lorry in the alleged accident to get compensation from the appellant/insurance company.
There was no nexus between the said lorry and the death of said deceased- Manik Jadhav.

. She further submitted that appellant/insurance company has filed application summoning the Hospital authorities as witness and to produce MLC along with entire case sheet and notice/summons, but they did not turn up to produce the same.
She further contended that the driver of the alleged vehicle i.e. lorry was not holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the particular type of vehicle as on the date of accident.
Hence, sought for allowing the appeal.
22. Learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that the claim petition cannot be dismissed on the ground of delay in lodging FIR.
In order to substantiate the same, the petitioners have produced FIR and charge-sheet and relied on decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Ravi vs Badrinarayan & Ors.

reported in (2011) 4 SCC 693.
23.
With regard to liability of insurance company is concerned, while deciding the issues, the Tribunal has properly discussed the evidence on record in accordance - 14 - with law.

Even on re-appreciation of the evidence on record and keeping in mind the decision of in Ravi vs Badrinarayan & Ors., referred to supra, I do not find any legal infirmities in the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.
Hence, I answered point No.2 in Negative.

(i) The appeal filed by the appellant/insurance company in MFA No.202011/2015 is dismissed.
(ii) The appeal filed by the petitioners in MFA No.201130/2015 is hereby allowed in part.

(iii) Appellants/petitioners are entitled for  compensation in a sum of Rs.11,25,000/- as against Rs.6,00,000/-
